importance_ranking.reason: Portable cabins have extreme visual sub-type variation — a 6×4 ft security booth, a 20×10 ft site office, a container-style cabin, and a double-storey accommodation block are visually distinct products. Buyers use the image to identify the correct product type before reading any text; wrong type is an immediate skip.

Product type (security / office / accommodation / storage) and size (L×W) are non-interchangeable primary shortlisting criteria — a buyer cannot substitute one for another. Material and insulation type further determine thermal performance and durability, which are critical for long-term site deployment.

Price varies substantially with product type, size, and material — a 6×4 ft MS security cabin and a 20×40 ft PUF-insulated accommodation block are orders of magnitude apart. Indian B2B buyers are price-aggressive and compare prices across sellers once spec equivalence is confirmed; listed price is a hard shortlisting gate.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Standard-size cabins are quoted per piece; large custom or multi-room builds are quoted per sq ft. Both units are active in the market — price cannot be compared without knowing which unit applies to a given listing.
importance_ranking.reason: Per piece vs per sq ft is a genuine market ambiguity confirmed across multiple manufacturer sites. A buyer comparing two listings without knowing the unit cannot determine which is cheaper; unit must be shown alongside price.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall exists in this category — siblings are material/type-based (MS Porta Cabin, FRP Cabin, GI Portable Cabin), not brand-based, and buyers search by product type and material rather than manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: Manufacturer vs trader distinction matters for installation support, customisation capability, and warranty — institutional and government buyers evaluate this during vendor selection. However, company ranks last as specs and price drive initial shortlisting.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines what the cabin IS — security, site office, accommodation, storage, toilet block — with non-interchangeable structural layouts, fittings, and the largest price delta across values in this category.

Physical footprint is non-interchangeable and price scales directly with area — a 6×4 ft security post and a 40×10 ft accommodation block cannot substitute for each other, making size the second-largest price driver after product type.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sandwich panel thickness (50mm / 75mm / 100mm) determines thermal insulation performance and structural rigidity — buyers in extreme climates specify this explicitly and it drives a meaningful price difference between otherwise identical cabins.

MS vs GI structural frame is a primary durability and corrosion-resistance differentiator — Agent 3 identifies this as a key buyer-facing attribute, and the existing 'Material' spec covers panel/cladding materials (ACP, FRP, PUF Panel), not the structural frame grade.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Routes the RFQ to sellers who manufacture the specific cabin type and material variant — a security cabin fabricator and a modular prefab accommodation supplier are different businesses, and this spec immediately determines seller fit.

Primary dimensional spec that determines cabin footprint and manufacturing feasibility — sellers need length (combined with width) to assess whether they can supply the required size and to provide an accurate price.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers need to know whether the buyer requires a site office, security cabin, accommodation block, storage unit, or toilet block — these are structurally distinct products that different manufacturers specialise in, and this is the single most important routing signal for accurate seller response.

PUF, EPS, rock wool, and FRP panels represent different thermal performance tiers and price points — sellers who specialise in PUF panel cabins may not supply FRP variants, making this a critical supplier-routing spec.
